source_title: PSA: Avoid Tremont, The Bryn & The Pointe
post_title: PSA: Avoid Tremont, The Bryn & The Pointe
post_body:
PSA: For Students Looking for Off-Campus Housing in STATE COLLEGE: AVOID TREMONT, THE BRYN & THE POINTE

TO ALL STUDENTS: Avoid renting an apartment from TREMONT, THE BRYN, or THE POINTE in State College, and any property managed or owned by CARDINAL GROUP COMPANIES or GREYSTAR.
predatory businesses,
that target college students. Although
reflects a "warning" on their website to avoid any association with properties that prohibit potential Tenants from viewing their apartment before Leasing, that is exactly what
employees do!
THE POINTE at 501 S. VAIRO
is a "slum property". They forbid potential Tenants from viewing apts before paying them multiple months of rent in advance, and signing a Lease. They only allow the view of a "Model", which is nothing like the actual apartments that look like "crack-houses". They scam people by making false representations about the
true conditions
of the apartments. Their Marketing Manager is
WENDY DONOVAN
. She lies to potential Tenants about everything. She has also stated that they will not, under any circumstance, allow potential renters to see their apartment before they actually take possession of it, even if the apt is vacant.
THE POINTE'S
Manager is
ZACH LOVETT.
He carries out the same RACKETEERING SCAM that
CARDINAL GROUP
, both on VAIRO.
These properties will lie to potential Tenants and say there is only 2 apts left and they need to put a deposit/sign a lease fast to ensure they have an apt. They'll ask for approximately 3 months rent, or multiple months, in far advance. In the Illinois case, the VICTIMS discovered that they'd paid for an apartment that did not exist, on the day the Victim Tenant moved-in. The apt was uninhabitable! There was
Black Mold
throughout, filthy, black carpets, although the Marketing Manager,
KATIE LIBERMAN LOVETT
said that the apt and ALL apts are "deep steam cleaned". She and other staff make false claims about doing extensive cleaning to avoid
COVID-19 exposure,
especially if a previous Tenant vacated in a short period of time before the new Tenant(s) moved in. This is also false! These misstatements and misrepresentations are all part of their
scheme to defraud.
THE POINTE
does the very same thing. Although they are owned and managed by different companies,
ZACH LOVETT, THE POINTE'S
KATIE LIBERMAN LOVETT, CARDINAL GROUP'S
former Marketing Mgr at
and current employee of
CARDINAL GROUP
, are married, and carried out the same
scheme to defraud.
These predatory businesses will take their time to repair/replace old, non-working appliances.
had ALL non-working appliances at the time the Plaintiff in the Illinois lawsuit moved in, although they claimed that they had ALL
updated and up-to-date appliances.
Their webpage reflects that as well, but the appliances were 25-27 years old and NOT working.
CARDINAL GROUP staff will then tell Tenants,
"Too bad! You signed a Lease! Pay us or we'll send you to collections!"
They will also delete Tenants MAINTENANCE WORK ORDERS so that there is not a "paper trail" and no evidence, in their efforts to further their scheme to defraud.
along with it's
Owner, HAIM SABAN, CARDINAL GROUP COMPANIES, CARDINAL GROUP MANAGEMENT,
CEO, ALEX O'BRIEN, KATIE LIBERMAN LOVETT,
VALERIE HERRERA
are being sued in the state of Illinois.
CARDINAL GROUP MGMT.
employee and worked/works at
If you're a Penn State student, or you know of any student who has been been defrauded / scammed by these people / predatory businesses, contact PSU's Student Legal Services.
*Do not contact
LAURA ROBBINS
*, Attorney in State College. She has claimed that she "handled" legal disputes on behalf of*
*. She's also a liar.*
Beware of Attorneys that don't "sound right".
It is also important that those who have been scammed by these people, file an online Complaint with the Pennsylvania Attorney General's Office. It takes about 7 minutes to complete!
***CARDINAL GROUP COMPANIES, ALEX O'BRIEN, and CARDINAL GROUP MANAGEMENT ARE ALSO BEING SUED IN DENVER, COLORADO for the same Racketeering Scheme, Scheme to Defraud!
***BEWARE OF ANY PROPERTY OWNED/OPERATED BY CARDINAL GROUP, OR GREYSTAR (HAS SIMILAR LAWSUITS AGAINST THEM).
Last, do your research. There are not many Student Housing properties Off-Campus, that have not been recently sued in the past, or have pending lawsuits against them by the Pennsylvania Attorney General, for defrauding and scamming college students!!! A quick "google search" or accessing their website, go in the upper-left-hand corner, enter "State College" in the Search bar. There, you can see some current cases. You can contact them directly as well. That online Complaint is important! They can't do anything unless they know about it
Here's an article about the Denver, Colorado Class Action Lawsuit against CARDINAL GROUP COMPANIES & MANAGEMENT:             https://coloradosun.com/2021/10/29/cardinal-group-management-lawsuit/   There's also posts on Reddit.
There are also positive Reviews for these slum-properties on Google and Yelp, by
staff members.
REMEMBER: SEE SOMETHING, SAY SOMETHING!! And contact an Attorney if you've been scammed by them!
4y ago
No clue if this this legit, but I've been jerked around by enough landlords in State College to say that it's at the very least, plausible.
How? Please elaborate for educational purposes... I will be looking for an apartment soon and your experiences may be helpful. Thanks.
I agree. Your post is indeed quite clear and elaborate. I actually requested regarding the comment above.
There are no good property management companies in State College for undergrads. There are decent buildings run by slumlords. There are terrible buildings. Don't rent sight unseen.
When I searched for rentals, it was very difficult to find properties that weren't being sued by the PA Atty. Gen! That's how bad it is. But is their fault. They're too lenient on these slumlords.
I currently live at The Bryn. I can confirm everything in this thread. Predatory Landlords has never been described so perfectly.
My roommate and I were fined $375 for switching rooms. EACH.
My shower never completely turns off, it is constantly dripping. Also the water gets so fucking hot, like burn your skin hot. It will randomly get like that in the shower too. Also, the toilet randomly overflows when flushed. Listen, Im a dude so trust me, at first I thought it was me. Nope, have taken pisses in it and had it overflow completely, then immediately flush like nothing happened. The countertops and cracks and creases in the kitchen are fucking filthy. The countertop in just about every room is peeling away.
Dont even get me started about the internet. Once a week it goes out. Of course though, The Bryn uses a third party ISP, who is absolutely useless. Call The Bryn office? We have contacted them and they are working on it. Theres nothing we can do. Heres there number. Call the ISP? Its up and running. Literally I had that parade of phone calls 5 times already, and Im halfway through the lease.
Bottom line is, DO NOT LIVE AT THE BRYN.
Hopefully you took photos of the filth that was already there when you moved in. They do not clean between Tenants. It's all a scam.
The Park is no fucking better. But Penn State does have free legal aid to students with housing issues- theyve been great.
Not sure what you're talking about. I've lived at the Park for 3 years and they've always worked with my with rent, I've always been able to see my lease before signing it, and they're more than willing to give tours of apartments that are close to the actual ones. They've helped me with rent confusion on multiple occasions and I've never had an experience this bad with them
They will dick you on move-out with bogus charges, but besides that I agree the Park was pretty okay
ve been hit with bogus move out charges. 300 dollars for a patch of dead grass on the lawn. (I spent no time in the yard so I knew this was horse shit.). I asked for a itemized list of expenses that amounted to 300 dollars that would cover reseeding a 2 square foot patch of grass. Said I wouldnt pay for this until that was produced, and that they could take me to small claims court if necessary. They said forget about it. Sometimes you just need to call them on their bullshit with a confident posture, and youll get fairer treatment.
I definitely think more students need to listen to this sort of advice. Sometimes these places are unavoidable because of cheaper rent. Always leave a paper trail, always ask for itemized lists, always take before and after photos and bother them to the point that they realize youre not the type for student they can leech off of. Once they realize you wont hand over the money right away like most students do without second thought, theyll drop it because its not worth their time to pester you than pursue another clueless student instead. Hate to put it that way, but it is what it is.
Not sure anyone will care, but avoid Continental at all costs... Took them 2 months to fix a leak coming from out kitchen ceiling and now it has a 3 inch bow in it...
Lived at Tremont for 3 years (2017-2020) and this is accurate. When we moved in my mom and my roommates moms just gasped when they saw the dump we moved into. Regardless, we cleaned it up and paid super cheap rent for 3 years.
Idk if this is some kind of fake spam message or if its legit, but all the random ass capitalization and bold words make you seem like an incompetent shit (or possibly a rival property management that wants more business lol)
I lived at the Bryn. Closet was infested with black mold when I moved in and nothing was done.
Report Black Mold in apts, and contact a toxic mold litigation attorney.
There are many lawyers in Pennsylvania that specialize in "toxic mold litigation"!
Lived at the Pointe for a year and liked it. I get OP probably had a bad experience but referring to the place as a "crack house" is extremely out of touch and privileged. Go touch some grass or something.
Lived at The Pointe for two years. I loved it. This is a big generalization and I never had an issue.
Same, it was really clean, spacious, furnished, and everyone had their own bedroom and bathroom. It had a small weight room with treadmills, an indoor half-court basketball court, outdoor basketball and tennis courts, and a pool. They gave out free snacks pretty much every week. And they 100% did apartment tours. They had people tour our apartment while we were living there.
The only reason I moved was because I wanted to live downtown for my senior year. The Pointe ended up being cheaper than my downtown apartment which was much smaller and I shared a bedroom and bathroom. It was also unfurnished and very old.
Same. I lived there for 2 years and they even lowered the rent for my renewal. My roommate from dorms also liked it there.
The rooms are decent sized, the common areas are okay. Usually maintenance is quick on priority items like toilet not working, AC broken, etc. Minor things you can just call up the front office and they'll usually send someone out.
I live at one of these properties and I don't really have many complaints. Did Zoom Uni from here last year and was happy enough to sign another year for this year. Obv be careful out there and I'm not saying OP didn't have bad experiences but in my experience I can't complain
Yeah, I lived at the Pointe and I had amicable-enough experience for two years there. I most often heard people bitch about communication with them, but I never had issues; I would just stop by the front office with my problems on my way in from campus. I also never had major concerns like leaks or broken HVAC, as a disclaimer. Mileage will always vary, and OP's right about not getting to see the specific apartments, but calling the places crack-houses is an extreme statement from a general experience of my friends and I.
I lived at the Pointe and I really enjoyed it. I'm sure there is some shady stuff going on and some people have worse experiences but I actually was very happy with my time there just a few years ago (2019-2020)
I lived at the Bryn for 6 months. When I moved in, it was nothing short of awful. It was clear it had not been cleaned in years, and they said they didnt clean the common areas cuz there was another tenant living there (he was like a ghost tho, just stayed in his room all day). The less said about the kitchen, the better. I tried arguing about the cleanliness but they asked me to pay 150$ for a cleanup. Obviously didnt, ended up spending 5 bucks at dollar tree and cleaning the shit up myself. The countertops were all coming off and were filthy, while the utilities in the unit were ancient. And then at the end they had the audacity to charge me for leaving stuff behind, like unused trash covers, as well a dustbin that was there from before I moved in. Horrible experience, please never live there. However, Im currently staying at the pointe and its been a good time so far. I actually have no complaints about the unit and the management yet, but its true they dont let you see the unit before move in. Lets hope I finish the remaining year without problems.
At THE BRYN, the newest appliance in my kid's apt was 26 years old. None were working at all. Maintenance gave us the lowdown of how the property was managed and how they commit "fraud". I wish this Reddit thing had the ability to upload audios. I was also told my a couple of "honest" staff that they purposely deleted Maintenance Work Orders so that there was not evidence and a papertrail. We did screen shots when posting anything immediatly, so even after they were deleted, we still had proof.
At THE POINTE they've also deleted information from the "Ledger" in the Resident Portal, from Tenants, so that there isn't proof of payments and charges, or the dates. These were at the time they demanded deposits and monthly rent in advance. All that was "deleted" by THE POINTE management. It was there in the beginning, but the Manager deleted them after Tenants moved in. He tried to blame it on a "glitch" and said he'd "look into it" and contact the company that "handles the portal". He's a liar though. He refused to give the name of the person or entity that "handles it." LOL What a lying POS. Thank goodness we have proof of our communications.
On a side note though, I stay in a 3 bed 3 bath, but my utilities are very high. Ive just been posted a bill for $132 per person for gas and electricity for January (thermostat is kept between 65-70). Is this a reasonable bill? I feel its very high and a very unfair reflection on our usage but then i cant really do anything about it.
I can attest to some of what OP is saying. I live at tremont and while I love my unit, I know a lot of friends that got screwed with theirs. Place wasn't clean when they moved in, apartments that were run down, etc. However, I got a renovated unit and our unit is by far the nicest. Yes it wasn't perfect when we moved in however it didn't take long to fix. Maintenance has been EXTREMELY responsive with ANY issue we had. We had a garbage disposal break and within 3 days it was fixed. We weren't charged anything for the service, and the employees followed covid protocols. Additionally, we are not asked for rent in advance or anything of the like. Due to the nature of off campus housing, most places are predatory towards students. Besides the apartment not being perfectly clean, nothing has been totally out of the ordinary for our renovated unit. I would really advise anyone living at these three places to pay the extra money for the renovated unit.
Can corroborate about the Bryn. Had a family member there. 90% awful. Most of the things in her apartment didn't work when she moved in. Her father had to threaten them to get them to fix things.
On the plus side: it's a good incentive to graduate as fast as you can.
Also, ARPM is pretty infamous, and McKinney is one of the best for onwership groups
